A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DecompDPO study. All 19 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original CrossDocked2020 generation, target-specific optimization, ablation and molecular-conformation results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original results, including revised generation experiments and additional physics-penalty ablations, validity checks and training analyses.

M1.justification: The GlobalDPO/LocalDPO combination, weighted objectives, geometry penalty, diffusion backbone and linear beta formula are retained. The corrected reward-sign expression matches v2's stated preference rule; the recombination argument and fragmentation description do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use CrossDocked2020 for general molecule generation and target-specific optimization. The added validity, molecular-size and training analyses reuse this coverage without introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MolCRAFT and the general-purpose optimizer TAGMol. The single-objective comparison adds KGDiff alongside the retained AliDiff in v3 Table 4. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparisons; RGA and DecompOpt remain the targeted-optimization baselines.

E3.justification: Generation fine-tuning changes from one epoch/16,000 steps in v2 Appendix C.3 to 30,000 steps in v3 Appendix B.4. v3 also adds molecular-size and PoseBuster/PoseCheck evaluation metrics and a control without the physics penalty. The principal dataset split and preference-pair count remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct physics-penalty ablation, broader physical-validity checks, atom-count versus docking-score analysis, empirical geometry distributions, preference-pair distributions and a training-success trajectory. These supplement the retained decomposition/beta ablations, decomposability evidence, trade-off plots and molecular examples.

E5.justification: Both versions use means, medians and distribution boxplots without specifying repeated-run counts, random seeds or significance tests. v3's strain-energy quartiles summarize an additional metric using descriptive distribution reporting; they do not establish a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Generation success rate changes from 36.2% to 43.9% and median High Affinity from 95.2% to 98.5%, with a longer fine-tuning budget. Single-objective success changes from 43.0% to 46.8%. Geometry results also change, including C–C distance JSD worsening from 0.426 to 0.535. Numerous validity and ablation results are added, while targeted-optimization Table 2 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds an algebraic reformulation of LocalDPO as GlobalDPO on recombined substructures under the existing factorization assumption, and the reward-sign expression is corrected. The new Equation 11 is problematic as written: multiplying binary membership indicators over all atoms makes its product zero for multi-fragment molecules.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the novelty claim from 'the first' to 'one of the first' and removes the corresponding priority assertion from the conclusion. Headline generation results are updated, while the central dual-granularity method and its two applications retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 attributes incidental QED/SA gains to reward correlations and acknowledges residual steric clashes. It removes v2's explicit limitations concerning objective coverage and weighted-sum optimization. Its new assertion of outperforming Molecule-level DPO on all metrics conflicts with the lower QED values in Table 5.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link and descriptions of RDKit/BRICS/AlphaSpace2 fragmentation and Opt Prior construction in Appendices B.3 and B.5. These disclose existing components more fully. The documented fine-tuning budget is also updated; most optimizer, hardware and preprocessing details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands discussion of guided SBDD optimization and ligand-only methods, adding works such as PILOT, TAGMol, KGDiff, REINVENT, GraphGA and Saturn. It explicitly explains the choice of 3D SBDD comparators and qualifies the priority claim. These changes extend research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanations and results discussion are extensively rewritten. Related work gains a separate optimization discussion, broader impacts moves into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized around theory, implementation and results. Author, affiliation and publication text also changes.

P2.justification: v3 adds conformation-summary, validity and ablation tables plus several diagnostic plots. Existing conformation plots are relocated and regrouped, and Figure 3's molecular panels are rearranged. The journal template changes typography and page layout, while benchmark tables gain grouping and molecular-size columns.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's indirect conformation evidence, v3 directly tests removal of the physics penalty in Tables 10–11 and adds broader validity checks in Table 9, strengthening support for a central component. Additional comparators and reproducibility details help. Removed limitations and new mathematical/prose inconsistencies temper these gains; higher headline scores under longer fine-tuning do not establish a same-setting advance.
